title: ApplicationInterface
description: An active-structure access point owned by an application component or collaboration, such as a mounted controller, gRPC server binding, GraphQL endpoint or message-channel listener, through which that component's application services are reachable by users or other components, through a channel of one kind (its interfaceType) and, where it has one, a named protocol. A library package's public entry point (the module its consumers import, as declared by an index file or an exports map) is an application interface too: one per entry point, whose interfaceType is in-process, assigned to the application services its exported functions and hooks offer. It is the channel itself, not the behaviour offered through it and not the formal contract document describing it; a programming-language interface, protocol or abstract class that only declares a service's operations (an IOrderService that other components depend on) is not an application interface because of the keyword. Use ApplicationService instead when the element describes the externally visible behaviour or functionality offered, such as 'order placement', independent of the endpoint, protocol or channel through which it is reached, including a language-level interface or dependency-injection contract that declares the operations offered. Use ApplicationComponent instead when the symbol is the deployable or replaceable module, service or package as a whole, rather than one of the access points it provides. Use ApplicationInteraction instead when the symbol represents joint behaviour carried out by two or more components exchanging messages, rather than the single access point one component offers. Use ApplicationFunction instead when the symbol is internal handler or business logic invoked behind the endpoint, rather than the endpoint binding or adapter itself.

documentation.description: Free-text description of the access point: which component provides it, its base path, address or channel name, the services reachable through it, and any notable constraints. Set it whenever the name and protocol alone do not identify the endpoint.

protocol.description: The named protocol the interface speaks, when it has one. Name the highest level that is itself a protocol: MCP for an MCP server (not JSON-RPC or HTTP), GraphQL for a GraphQL endpoint, and likewise gRPC, SOAP, JSON-RPC, WebSocket, SSE, AMQP, MQTT, Kafka or NATS; HTTP for a plain HTTP API. REST is an architectural style, not a protocol: a REST API's protocol is HTTP. Transport and security are not part of it: an HTTPS endpoint's protocol is HTTP, and TLS, TCP and the like belong in the technology layer. Spell it as the protocol's own documentation does. The set of protocols is open; leave it unset where interfaceType says all there is, such as an in-process entry point or a user interface.

interfaceType.description: The kind of channel the interface is, by who or what reaches it and how. api: a program calls it across a process boundary, over the network or a local channel such as standard input and output or a socket (an HTTP, gRPC, GraphQL, JSON-RPC or MCP endpoint, a WebSocket). message-channel: a queue or topic on a broker that the component consumes from or publishes to (AMQP, MQTT, Kafka, NATS). in-process: a library's public entry point, imported into the consumer's own process (its index file or exports map). command-line: a command that people or scripts run, with its arguments, standard input and output, and exit code. user-interface: the screens or pages a person uses (a web, desktop or terminal UI). file-exchange: files the component reads from or writes to an agreed location for another party (a batch drop folder, an SFTP inbox). The exchange pattern (request-reply, publish-subscribe) is not this attribute: it belongs to the ApplicationInteraction and ApplicationService the interface takes part in.

x-dr-evidence: A controller or router class that groups route handlers under a base path and is mounted on a web server, such as a Spring @RestController with @RequestMapping("/orders"), an Express Router passed to app.use('/orders', ...), or a FastAPI APIRouter included in the app.
A gRPC servicer or GraphQL schema/resolver set registered on a server at startup, such as add_OrderServiceServicer_to_server(...) or an Apollo server exposing /graphql.

A message or socket entry point bound to a named channel in code or config, such as a @RabbitListener(queues="orders") consumer, an AMQP queue binding in application.yml, or a WebSocket endpoint handler (@ServerEndpoint, socket.io namespace).
